title: I Used the Arcade Token Hopper Clock on the Attendant Who Palmed Credits

parts.text: I paid hopper 7 at 4:36 p.m. and attendant Sol palmed a staff key into my unpaid-looking leftover credits. The cabinet said: PAY THE HOPPER. NO STAFF KEYS. END ON ZERO. I was twenty-three, player, holding a receipt. Sol shrugged. "Attendants are the games." I photographed the cabinet, the receipt, and the key in the slot. Then I asked for the hopper log. At 4:42 the owner pinged why Sol's name was on palmed credits. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Sol's staff key in hopper 7 during my paid credits.

social.video_title: The attendant palmed a staff key into my hopper — Part 1/2
social.description: Arcade, a paid hopper, a staff key in the slot. I logged the palm. Would you have asked the owner?

parts.text: Sol called it testing until the owner asked for the still. I printed the log, the cabinet, and the receipt. The key came out. Sol ran hoppers to zero and told the next attendant testing was always about optics. Optics is a word attendants use when receipts exist. Clock policy now has a second line: KEYS ARE NOT CREDITS. I keep hopper 7. Sol brown-bags the jokes. The cabinet finally looks like a receipt, not a pocket. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Hopper log, key out, and a second line. Was testing ever my credits?
